subject: Civic Education
competence: Broad curriculum competency standard in plain English
lesson: Expresses views about the available opportunities for vocational training: Courtroom / Citizen Grievance Tribunal: Competency Level 8.6.4
unique_learning_outcome: Expresses views about the available opportunities for vocational training.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: Imagine you are a young Sri Lankan citizen seeking vocational training to enhance your career prospects. You are part of a citizen grievance tribunal, and your role is to express views about the available opportunities for vocational training. Your team will take on different roles to investigate and decide on a reasoned solution.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher introduces the scenario and distributes the task aids, including the 'Role Cards' and 'Vocational Training Opportunities' handout. Students take on their assigned roles and organize their investigation.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students begin to discuss and investigate the scenario, using the role cards and handout to guide their decision-making. The teacher circulates to scaffold understanding and provide outcome-focused prompts.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Role Cards, 'Vocational Training Opportunities' handout, Chalkboard

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher facilitates student discussions, asking probing questions to scaffold understanding and encourage critical thinking. Students continue to investigate and debate the scenario.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students engage in roleplay, using the scenario to explore the available opportunities for vocational training. They discuss and debate the importance of trained labor and its impact on the local job market.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moderates student presentations, providing feedback and guidance on their reasoning and decision-making. Students present their group's findings and decisions.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Students present their group's findings and decisions, using visual aids and roleplay to illustrate their reasoning. The class provides peer feedback and evaluates the presentations.

summary: Students will express views about the available opportunities for vocational training through a simulated citizen grievance tribunal, taking on different roles and making decisions based on the scenario.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative feedback criteria: Students' ability to articulate their views on vocational training opportunities, their understanding of the importance of trained labor, and their ability to work collaboratively in a simulated citizen grievance tribunal.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: In-class quiz: Students will be asked to recall the main points discussed during the activity and provide a brief summary of the available opportunities for vocational training.

Activity: Courtroom / Citizen Grievance Tribunal: Competency Level 8.6.4
Approach: Students use courtroom / citizen grievance tribunal to explore 'Expresses views about the available opportunities for vocational training.'. Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Student task: Students take civic roles, respond to a shared scenario, and agree on a reasoned decision. Standard class layout (40 students): Desks arranged into 8 teams (8 teams (8 groups of 5)), with students rotating responsibilities (Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer) without bystanders.
Teacher facilitation: Organizes all 40 students using 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer. and monitors progress with outcome-focused prompts and time checks. Circulates across 8 teams, facilitating role execution and formatively checking progress.
Expected output: A short role-based civic decision and its reasons.
Grouping: 8 teams (8 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
